 Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle Sr., reportedly charged in the Philippines with possession of child sexual abuse material
 The charges come as the duchess's estranged father is in U.S. custody facing similar charges. 
 Jasmine Andersson , Anthony Rivas Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:05 PM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Meghan Markle said she was first made aware of the allegations against her father by London’s Metropolitan Police in 2019. (Jonathan Brady/Pool PA via AP) Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., has reportedly been charged with possession of child sexual abuse material in the Philippines, less than two weeks after he was arrested in the United States on similar charges.
 Markle Sr. was charged by the Philippine National Police with two counts of offering, distributing, selling, exporting or importing child sexual abuse material and one count of possessing it, according to multiple media outlets . ITV News reports that prosecutors are evaluating the charges as they determine whether to issue a subpoena.
 The charges come after the FBI arrested him in a separate investigation on Nov. 6 in Lakeland, Fla. , on charges related to child sexual abuse material linked to storage units in Los Angeles.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Sun first reported in October that Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr., had told Philippine police that after his father left the Philippines in May, he discovered images of child sexual abuse material among boxes at his father's former home in Cebu. Philippine police had named Markle Jr. a "person of interest" in the investigation but later retracted the allegation and apologized to him, saying the matter had been "cleared up," according to a later report by The Sun.
 Markle Sr., 82, had been under investigation in the Philippines since October over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse material. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla told the AFP that police inspected Markle Sr.'s former home in Cebu following his son's report, where he said they found a "trove" of suspected child sexual abuse material and a laptop.
 Markle Sr. has vehemently denied the allegations against him, telling the British newspaper the Daily Mail on Oct. 23: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick."
 In that interview with the Daily Mail , he said the computers had not been in his possession since he left Mexico in January 2025 and that he did not know who had access to them. He said he would welcome a forensic examination of the devices.
 Advertisement Advertisement In a separate interview with the Daily Mail's sister paper, the Mail, he said: "I have never had sex with anyone under the age of 18." He added that if there was anything bad on his devices, "it was put there by someone else," according to the British newspaper the Daily Telegraph .
 Remulla told the British newspaper the Guardian on Oct. 25 that investigators were considering all angles because the case involved a family dispute, while stressing that a full forensic examination would give a "definitive picture."
 The FBI previously told Yahoo it was "aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of U.S. law."
 After his arrest on Nov. 6, Markle Sr. was released and placed on house arrest at the care home in Florida where he was arrested. However, he was taken back into U.S. custody on Nov. 10 after cutting off his ankle monitor. Police in the Philippines, meanwhile, say they are still investigating and additional charges could follow.
 Meghan was sent letter containing allegations in 2019
 After the allegations in the Philippines came to light, Meghan said in a public statement issued on Oct. 23 that she was "deeply distressed" by the allegations that had emerged against her father. "My thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," she said.
 Advertisement Advertisement It subsequently emerged that officers at London's Metropolitan Police passed on a letter to Meghan in early 2019 that informed of her of allegations about her father.
 "It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said. British police said it had not shared the letter with other law enforcement agencies.
 According to the Sun , Meghan was advised that speaking publicly could jeopardize any potential legal case.
 Addressing her decision to keep Archie and Lilibet away from their grandfather over the past few years, Meghan said that "any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them."
 Advertisement Advertisement She added: "My sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."
 Meghan reportedly wrote to her estranged father in December 2025 to tell him she was aware of child abuse allegations against him and would not allow him to meet his grandchildren. Meghan reportedly told her father the letter would be the last time he heard from her.
 According to the Sun , and also reported by the BBC and the Daily Telegraph , the Duchess of Sussex sent the letter to Thomas Markle while he was hospitalized in the Philippines following a leg amputation in December 2025 after a blood clot.
